title: Scatter plots and trend lines
explanation: A **scatter plot** shows whether two numbers move together, like study minutes and quiz scores. Adding a **trend line** makes the pattern clear. This uses `study_log` again.

tasks.prompt: Plot minutes on x and score on y with geom_point().
hints: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score)) + geom_point()
tasks.answer: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score)) + geom_point()

hints: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score, color = subject)) + geom_point()
tasks.answer: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score, color = subject)) + geom_point()

tasks.teach: **geom_smooth(method = "lm")** draws the best straight line through the points, with a grey band showing how uncertain it is. If color were in the main aes(), you'd get one line per subject instead. You'll meet "lm" again in Level 7.
tasks.prompt: Last one: add a straight trend line through all the points: + geom_smooth(method = "lm"). Keep it to one line by leaving color out of the main aes().
hints: method = "lm" means a straight line (a linear model).
ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm")
tasks.answer: ggplot(study_log, aes(x = minutes, y = score)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm")

recap: geom_point() makes scatter plots, color splits points by group, and geom_smooth(method = "lm") adds a straight trend line.
